answer: Each challenge is derived with domain-separated hashing from a specified future drand quicknet round, so its unpredictable threshold-BLS pulse fixes the task only after participants commit; mesa, yarrow, and trellis may denote distinct challenge families. Responses must bind the pulse and commitment, blocking precomputation and reusable offline work. Per-identity quotas or costly admission still constrain parallel Sybil attempts; beacon unpredictability alone does not identify unique actors.
